more.why: The read filings already show a consistent, well-documented picture of going-concern doubt, widespread defaults, a lien on all assets, about $4.75M due February 28, 2024, and only tiny, highly dilutive financing; the unread filings are mostly mid-2023 press-release 8-Ks and older 2021–2022 reports that would not change this view.

assessment.answer: The score sits in the 0.5-0.7 band mainly because net income is extremely negative against a tiny asset base (annualized -$31.0M against $2.9M of assets, 5th peer percentile) and liabilities are 8.2x assets. Two inputs likely held it below 0.7: operating cash burn improved sharply, and the annualized loss is no worse than a year earlier. The filings show distress well beyond what those 8 numbers capture. The company had $6,759 of cash, was in default on most of its notes and its PPP loan, and owes about $4.75M of debentures on February 28, 2024. Its recent raises were only tens of thousands of dollars.
moved_by: Cash of $6,759 at 9/30/2023 against a working capital deficit of $21.3M, so there is essentially no liquidity buffer
Widespread payment defaults: July 2022 senior secured notes ($2.27M principal), May 2022 notes, PPP loan, many merchant-style notes, and the Dec 2022, Jan 2023 and Feb 2023 debentures
About $4.75M of debentures ($2,485,000 + $2,267,140) now fall due together on February 28, 2024, with no visible way to pay
New monthly amortization from Nov/Dec 2023 (about $47k + $45k + $11k per month) that current cash cannot cover
Post-quarter financing was tiny and at sub-2-cent prices ($75,000 equity line draw, $20,500 PIPE, $100,000 note), and conversion prices were cut to $0.025
Secured debenture holders have a first-priority lien on all assets, and the Lind Global suit (>$920k) is proceeding after the motion to dismiss was denied
Late-filing pattern, and the CFO resigned in October 2023 with the CEO taking over the role

chart_plan.point: Chart 3 is clear and not misleading. Both axes say they are log or symlog, the 1x line marks where liabilities equal assets, the peer medians are labelled, and Creatd's 8.2x liabilities and 1,073% loss match the assessment. The six peers in the distressed corner are visible, so the title's 'among the worst, not uniquely the worst' holds. The three charts cover liquidity, balance-sheet history and peer standing, which is enough. I am not adding a loss-split chart because the stated non-cash items ($8.3M + $4.3M) do not reconcile with the stated cash-adjusted loss (-$14.9M) and the 36% share, so it would risk showing inconsistent numbers.
